Turkey is ready to host a meeting between Ukrainian and Russian leaders, President Erdogan said and reiterated the need for an urgent cease-fire. (All dailies reported)

 

Negotiations between Russia and Ukraine held this week in Istanbul have given meaningful impetus to efforts to end the war, President Erdogan said in a phone call with his Ukrainian counterpart Zelenskyy. (All digital media outlets reported)

 

The price of household natural gas was raised 35%, natural gas used for electricity generation 44.30%, and natural gas used outside of electricity generation in industry 50%.(All digital media outlets reported)

 

Parliament passed a law that lowers the election threshold for political parties from 10% to 7%, in addition to changes in requirements for parties to take part in polls and the formation of electoral boards. (All digital media outlets reported)

 

The VAT on basic necessities has been cut to 8%, in a change reflected in price tags starting today. (NTV)

 

Turkey registered 14,336 more coronavirus infections over the past 24 hours, according to Health Ministry data. The death toll grew 56 to 98,033, the ministry announced. As many as 272,196 tests for the virus were done over the past day.

 

 

SUMMARIES

EUD

 

The Strengthening the Effectiveness of National Asylum Procedures in accordance with International Standards and National Legislation project, carried out in cooperation with the UNHCR and the Interior Ministry Migration Management Directorate and funded by the European Union, was launched. Head of the Delegation of the EU to Turkey Ambassador Nikolaus Meyer-Landrut said that 4 million people had already been forced to flee their countries in Ukraine and that 6.5 million had been internally displaced, adding, Turkey is one of our biggest stakeholders in this context." Emphasizing that their financial cooperation with Turkey on migration management is not limited to recent crises and migration flows, Meyer-Landrut said this effort has a history dating back more than 10 years. Meyer-Landrut said since its establishment the Migration Management Directorate has placed importance on the compatibility of EU national asylum procedures with European and international standards.

Overview

Nearly 20 digital outlets reported the story. The outreach is around 900.000.

 

Head of the Delegation of the EU to Turkey Meyer-Landrut said, "Last autumn, Turkey approved the Paris Climate Agreement. This was truly a welcome development." Meyer-Landrut said that the agreement meant that Turkey now had a duty to begin fulfilling its commitments. He said that extra efforts are needed to save the planet, under the heavy impact of climate change, and that the support of all states, institutions, the private sector, ordinary citizens, and young people is needed.

 

The EU and Turkey are in contact to tackle the problem of waste traffic around the world, said Ambassador Nikolaus Meyer-Landrut, the head of the European Union Delegation to Turkey.

This is an issue that needs to be urgently solved. The European Union is currently developing a strategy on this issue and is working on steps to decrease this waste traffic, he told a climate summit at the Congresium Ankara ATO International Convention and Exhibition Center. In order to achieve this, we have to work together with the countries concerned. We have to change this pattern of waste being shipped around the world, he added. The ambassador elaborated that one of the areas the EU is working on is reducing the amount of waste by focusing on material that can be reused or ensuring that equipment is made in a way that lasts longer. Reducing packaging material is one of these steps, he added.

 

Overview

Daily Sabah (13,000) and Hurriyet Ankara (196.193) reported the story with an outreach of around 836,000. In addition, nearly 55 digital outlets reported the story. The total outreach is around 4.15 million.

 

 

5 women entrepreneurs supported by Hepsiburada, participating in the Business World Meetings organized for the second time under the Entrepreneurial Capacities Improvement Project for Sustainable Socio-Economic Integration (ENHANCER), opened a booth and introduced their brands. Deputy Industry and Technology Minister Çetin Ali Dönmez, Head of European Union Delegation Nikolaus Meyer-Landrut, and ICMPD Migration and Cooperation Director Martijn Pluim also visited the stands and met with entrepreneurs.

Overview

Balikesir Manset (circulation 480) highlighted the story with an outreach of around 1,900.  In addition, nearly 50 digital outlets reported the story. The total outreach is around 4 million.

 

 

TURKEY, EU AND EU MEMBER STATES

FM Cavusoglu said, Turkey is one of the countries that contributex the most to the European Union security. The EU shouldn t forget this quickly. The EU draws closer when they need something, then distances itself. Acting like this, can they become a global actor? No, they can t. What are the obstacles to modernization of the Customs Union agreement? Political. They're saying let's start the high-level dialogue. What was the obstacle before? You used to invite us. (A Haber)

 

Interior Minister Suleyman Soylu doubled down on his claim that CHP Chair Kemal Kilicdaroglu sent the joint declaration of 6 party leaders to a foreign ambassador to be checked. "You can't have an ambassador who's with you deliver a document to an EU ambassador to be vetted. It's treason," he said. (Haberturk)

 

Italian PM Mario Draghi said Turkey has played a crucial role in starting the Russia-Ukraine negotiation process, and that all countries are ready to cooperate with Turkey in this direction. (Anadolu Agency)

 

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, stating that the war between Russia and Ukraine will affect Turkey's growth expectation for 2022, lowered its forecast by 1.5 percentage points to 2%. (Karar)

 

Two people were killed after a gunman opened fire in a McDonald s in the northern Dutch city of Zwolle, according to police and local media. A 32-year-old suspect who claimed responsibility for the attack was arrested. (T24)

 

TRNC president Ersin Tatar said, "In the happiness and pride of being a state, we will never go back to before 1974. We will not give up Turkey's guarantorship." (Hurriyet)

 

Journalist Arzu Cakir wrote for VOA, "Developments in the Russian and Ukrainian crisis have re-highlighted Turkey's importance as a geopolitical actor. By standing at an equal distance from the two warring countries and hosting peace talks, Turkey positioned itself as a balance-minded force on the axis of NATO, the EU, Russia, and Ukraine. French President Macron, whose relations were recently strained enough to send a warship against Turkey in the Mediterranean, talks with President Erdogan at every opportunity, both face-to-face and on the phone.

 

On Interior Minister Suleyman Soylu s claims, Sabah columnist Hasmet Babaoglu wrote, Party leaders and executive committees depend on the ambassadors ... If the state thinks that the world is changing, the EU will eventually change, it s wrong. Whatever the European Union was in 2013, 2015, or July 15, 2016, it now has the same mentality ... Look at its ambassadors and understand ... This is the EU. It also does its best not to allow the formation of a great and powerful Turkey. This doesn t change. Let's not fool ourselves anymore.

 

 

MIGRANTS & REFUGEES

 

Pro-government daily Yeni Akit accusing the EU of being unfair, saying, Poland, which was flooded with refugees due to the war in Ukraine, requested financial aid from the European Union on the 35th day of the war and is about to receive the help it wants. On the other hand, Turkey, which has hosted 5 million Syrians for 11 years, was able to receive only a small part of the aid promised over the years.

 

An Education Ministry report said 730,000 of some one million Syrian children in Turkey go to school, but 35% are deprived of education. (DW Turkce)

 

In an exchange with a young Syrian while visiting tradesmen in Istanbul's Esenyurt district, which has a large population of foreign nationals, Victory Party leader Umit Ozdag said, "We will make sure to return you to the land of your fathers and grandfathers." (T24)

 

Haberturk columnist Fatih Altayli wrote, 190,000 Syrians have reportedly been granted 'exceptional citizen' status. Based on what justification, it isn't clear. Polls show that 77.6% of Turks feel that we have nothing in common culturally with Syrians. 91% of the Turkish public believe that at least half of Syrians will never return to their home country, even if things get back to normal in Syria. 84.7% of the public, meanwhile, want to see Syrians segregated. 77.9% of our citizens do not believe we can live alongside Syrian migrants in peace. And here's the real kicker. 77.8% of migrants say they don't intend to go back to Syria under any circumstances .

 

RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

Speaking to reporters during an official visit to Uzbekistan, Erdogan said that he believes that the meetings held this week by the Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Istanbul gave meaningful impetus to the peace process. (All dailies reported)

 

FM Mevlut Cavusoglu said Ukraine has given assurances on its position on neutrality and not joining NATO and that the two sides are now working on assurances. Cavusoglu also said Russia does not oppose Turkey and Germany acting as guarantors for Ukraine, but it is out of the question for Turkey to send troops and get involved in the war if it becomes a guarantor country, rejecting claims made in some reports. (Daily Sabah)

 

Kyiv, Moscow agree to having Turkey among guarantors of any potential peace deal, says FM Mevlut Cavusoglu. Both Russia and Ukraine consider Turkey an objective and balanced country that wants to play a constructive role in peace efforts, he said. (All digital outlets reported)

 

Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said on Twitter, Had another conversation with a real friend of Ukraine, President of Turkey Erdogan. Noted the high level of organization of negotiations of delegations in Istanbul. Agreed on further steps towards peace. Thanked for the readiness of Turkey to become the guarantor of security of our state!

 

FM Mevlut Cavusoglu discussed the latest situation in Ukraine on the phone with his Slovenian counterpart Anze Logar. (TRTHaber)

 

Ukrainian Defense Minister Reznikov said he was very proud to be a guest of President Erdogan in Istanbul, where came for the Russia-Ukraine negotiations. (Hurriyet)

 

NATO Secretary General Stoltenberg thanked Turkey for the peace talks held in Istanbul. (Cumhuriyet)

 

A French Defense Ministry delegation held talks in Ankara. It was reported that an air defense project within the scope of tripartite cooperation group between Turkey, Italy and France was on the table. (CNN Turk)

 

Russia, which has so far refused to walk back its 2014 annexation of Crimea, gave a positive signal for the first time at the Istanbul summit, reported Turkiye Gazetesi.

 

France-based magazine Contrepoints reported that France lost its mediation role to Turkey in the Ukraine-Russia negotiations. (TRTHaber)

 

President Erdogan may win the Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to reach a solution amid Russia s invasion of Ukraine, journalist Saskia van Westhreenen said in an article in the Dutch daily Algemeen Dagblad. (Daily Sabah)

 

Hurriyet columnist Abdulkadir Selvi worte, Turkey's sincere efforts and Erdogan's leadership are like a light in the middle of the darkness right now. This position of Turkey is watched and appreciated by the world. If Erdogan can make Putin and Zelenskyy sign a deal that will end the war and bring peace, then he deserves the Nobel Peace Prize.

 

The Guardian s diplomatic editor Patrick Wintour wrote, Among the pack of countries vying to act as mediators in the Russia-Ukraine war, Turkey has emerged as the winner, increasing the stature of Turkish diplomacy even if at this stage the theatrics may be well ahead of any solid outcome. Turkey s next aim is to get Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Putin in the same room in the next fortnight. If Turkey pulls it off, it would be an extraordinary turnaround for Erdogan, whose autocratic tendencies had threatened to make him an international pariah.

 

INTERNATIONAL

 

Cost calculations have shown that Turkey is the most affordable route for exports of Israeli natural gas, President Erdogan said. (NTV)

 

Azerbaijan fully abides by the terms of the trilateral deal signed with Russia and Armenia, President Erdogan said, calling on Armenia to also abide by the terms. (Daily Sabah)

 

There are important steps being taken to fix ties with Saudi Arabia, FM Mevlut Cavusoglu said. (A Haber)

 

A Turkish prosecutor asked an Istanbul court to dismiss a case into the gruesome 2108 murder of Riyadh critic Jamal Khashoggi and transfer it to Saudi Arabia. (All digital media outlets reported)

 

Israeli PM Naftali Bennett may visit Ankara after FM Cavusoglu's visit to Tel Aviv, says Rabbi Schneier.  (Anadolu Agency)

 

Turkey expressed regret that North Macedonia "ignored" calls by the Turkish community for the "fairly and transparent" conduct of a census in the Balkan country. (Anadolu Agency)

 

 

Turkey sent 80 tons of foodstuffs and mechanical spare parts for cars to the Lebanese army. (Anadolu Agency)

 

The Turkey Diyanet Foundation (TDV) delivered 2,500 food aid boxes to needy families in various areas of Sudan ahead of the Muslim holy month of Ramadan. (Anadolu Agency)

 

DOMESTIC POLITICS

CHP Chair Kemal Kilicdaroglu hit back at President Erdogan saying, "He's a tax officer. But I'm an economist. That's what sets us apart." Kilicdaroglureplied, "You're not an economist; at best, you're a collector for the syndicate of 5. A collector who has his eyes on the people's money."

 

CHP leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu pledged to solve all of the country's problems within 5 years if they come to power, saying, "You'll say, 'thank goodness for the alliance; thank goodness they're the ones running Turkey'." (Karar)

 

CHP leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu said, "No matter what obstacle they put, we re determined to bring Turkey to the light." (Birgun)

 

Future Party Chair Davutoglu said he was confident his party would achieve victory in the next elections, adding, "Don't bother pushing back. We're coming and you're going. You'll take all of your corruption, injustices, and nepotism with you when you go. (Karar)

 

Former HDP Mayor Ayhan Bilgen submitted a petition to the Interior Ministry to form Turkey s Voice Party (SES Party). Saying the party program aims to address Turkey s fundamental problems and provide suggestions for solutions, founding party member Muslum Dogan added that it seeks to develop democracy and respond to the peoples needs. (Daily Sabah)

 

CHP Deputy Utku Cakirozer said that at least 50 journalists were made to testify in court in March for their news reporting and opinions. (Diken)

 

A lawyer of the Istanbul Bar Association filed a second lawsuit against the Health Ministry for the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to be considered a mandatory vaccine and therefore be offered for free. (Duvar English)

 

Turkey plays a role in raising awareness of climate change worldwide, Deputy FM Yavuz Selim Kiran said. (Anadolu Agency)

 

An unlawful directive that was issued to supply coal to a geothermal plant run by the company Limak has come into force. Villagers trying to prevent centuries-old olive trees from being cut down were handcuffed and taken into police custody. (Sozcu)

 

Turkey s Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque in Istanbul will hold its first tarawih prayer in 88 years, a special evening prayer during the Muslim fasting month of Ramadan. (Yeni Akit)

THE ECONOMY

 

Turkey has no plans to increase the minimum wage for a second time in less than six months after a surge in inflation, Labour and Social Security Minister Vedat Bilgin said. (Sabah)

 

Energy and Natural Resources Minister Fatih Donmez said, "The reconciliation fee for natural gas and imported coal plants has been set at TL2,500/mWh. TL200 was agreed for other plants. With these subsidies, we will also ensure rising prices don't drive up consumer bills." (Hurriyet)

 

The foreign trade deficit reached $7.9 billion in February, the statistical authority announced. The gap widened significantly 135.5% from the corresponding month last year due to a surge in prices of energy, which constitutes nearly one-third of Turkey s imports, TurkStat said in a statement. (BloombergHT)

 

The World Bank has approved a $341 million funding package for Turkey to support a competitive agricultural sector and to promote climate-friendly technologies and practices in the country's various provinces. (Dunya)

 

Turkseker increased the price of sugar by 31%. (Sozcu)

 

SECURITY NEWS

 

In a raid on an address in Eyupsultan, Istanbul, 25 tons of counterfeit detergent was seized with a market value of 250,000 TL. (Beyaz Gazete)

 

WHAT IS EXPECTED?

President Erdogan will attend the opening of the Young Projects in Fatih program to be held at the Istanbul Fatih Municipality Central Library.

 

FM Mevlut Çavu_o lu will hold a joint press conference with Colombian Vice President and Foreign Minister Marta Lucia Ramirez.

 

Interior Minister Suleyman Soylu will attend the AA War Correspondents Training Certificate Ceremony.

 

Religious Affairs Directorate head Ali Erbas will lead tarawih prayers at Istanbul s Hagia Sophia Mosque.

 

Education Minister Mahmut Ozer will take part in the program Vocational High Schools Meet with Families.

 

Industry and Technology Minister Mustafa Varank will attend the Local Administrations Science Centers Support Program signing ceremony.

Journalist Engin Eren will face trial in Batman on charges of terrorist group membership.

SUMMARIES

EUD

 

The Strengthening the Effectiveness of National Asylum Procedures in accordance with International Standards and National Legislation project, carried out in cooperation with the UNHCR and the Interior Ministry Migration Management Directorate and funded by the European Union, was launched. Head of the Delegation of the EU to Turkey Ambassador Nikolaus Meyer-Landrut said that 4 million people had already been forced to flee their countries in Ukraine and that 6.5 million had been internally displaced, adding, Turkey is one of our biggest stakeholders in this context." Emphasizing that their financial cooperation with Turkey on migration management is not limited to recent crises and migration flows, Meyer-Landrut said this effort has a history dating back more than 10 years. Meyer-Landrut said since its establishment the Migration Management Directorate has placed importance on the compatibility of EU national asylum procedures with European and international standards.

Overview

Nearly 20 digital outlets reported the story. The outreach is around 900.000.

 

Head of the Delegation of the EU to Turkey Meyer-Landrut said, "Last autumn, Turkey approved the Paris Climate Agreement. This was truly a welcome development." Meyer-Landrut said that the agreement meant that Turkey now had a duty to begin fulfilling its commitments. He said that extra efforts are needed to save the planet, under the heavy impact of climate change, and that the support of all states, institutions, the private sector, ordinary citizens, and young people is needed.

 

The EU and Turkey are in contact to tackle the problem of waste traffic around the world, said Ambassador Nikolaus Meyer-Landrut, the head of the European Union Delegation to Turkey.

This is an issue that needs to be urgently solved. The European Union is currently developing a strategy on this issue and is working on steps to decrease this waste traffic, he told a climate summit at the Congresium Ankara ATO International Convention and Exhibition Center. In order to achieve this, we have to work together with the countries concerned. We have to change this pattern of waste being shipped around the world, he added. The ambassador elaborated that one of the areas the EU is working on is reducing the amount of waste by focusing on material that can be reused or ensuring that equipment is made in a way that lasts longer. Reducing packaging material is one of these steps, he added.
